transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
End: 16:46 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Stellarnet Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Platform), Hannah Lee (Finance), Omar Nadeem (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR / health sync. 3rd month into pilot. Discussed Feb reliability blips, cost spikes on peak token storms, and plan for Dedicated benchmark. Agreed to share security docs and schedule a 2-hour benchmark window.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): okay thanks everyone for joining, uh we'll call this the operational sprint and adoption playbook sync for Stellarnet, try and keep to 45 minutes, got the agenda in the invite
00:16 Lena (Stellarnet - Head of ML): thanks Maya, yeah we're down, got a couple of folks on the platform side and finance. we had some surprises in feb so want to make sure we cover reliability then next steps for Dedicated pilot
00:29 Arjun (Redwood SE): great, quick ground rules — we'll surface the incidents, tradeoffs and then go through a bench plan. i have sample configs ready.
00:42 Samir (Stellarnet - Platform Eng): quick context, our traffic is spiky, daily peak 11am-1pm PST, and last month we hit a 3x token storm during a marketing push which triggered auto scale and we saw 800ms p50 go up to 1.9s for a 5-10 minute window
01:05 Maya: ok that's useful. um recap — you're at Hosted today, right? using the redwood public api with pinned model variant 'rdw-m-13b-quant'?
01:18 Lena: yes hosted with the 13b quant, though our prod route uses some prefix caching, but a lot of the longer responses bypass the cache so cost spiked.
01:33 Hannah (Finance): and that spike translated to a larger bill, we need predictability. looking for a path to a committed model footprint if it reduces unit cost
01:45 Arjun: totally. Dedicated generally gives you more predictable throughput and better cost per token at sustained qps. but the tradeoff is commit size and management. we can run a benchmark to show unit economics at your peak profile
02:02 Omar (SRE): security is a gating factor for us — how does key mgmt work? can we bring our KMS? what about audit logs and retention?
02:18 Diego (Redwood CSM): we can definitely run through the KMS and audit log options, we support customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated and can send the SOC2 and network diagrams after the call
02:31 Lena: perfect. also curious about fallbacks — if Dedicated nodes hit some degraded perf, do we auto-fail to hosted?
02:45 Arjun: yes that's in the routing policies, you can set a priority order — Dedicated first then hosted as fallback. the routing has region and model-compat checks. sometimes the product name shows up in docs as "Redwood Dedicated" or the internal short 'ded' which i think some transcriptions get wrong
03:05 Samir: concretely, we need to know what's the p99 we can expect at our 200 qps sustained and bursts to 400 qps for 2 mins. also how batching configs will affect latencies
03:22 Arjun: i'll propose a two-phase bench. Phase A: repro traffic on Hosted with your exact prompts to measure baseline p50/p95/p99 and token costs. Phase B: run on Dedicated 4xA100-ish (or equivalent) with batching configs and quant profiles. we'll capture token/sec, GPU utilization, and p99 under burst
03:44 Maya: that gives you the delta and costs for a committed monthly quote vs current usage based charge
03:55 Hannah: yes we need that number. also include forecasted 3-months spend with and without prefix caching tweaks
04:10 Lena: on reliability — in Feb we had two incidents. one was a degraded KV cache hit rate drop after a model rollout, the other was a short network flapping with a partner region. any learnings?
04:28 Arjun: the kv cache regression is unfortunately a common gotcha when a model changes tokenization or response framing; we recommend pinning a stable model during rollouts and running a canary against a small traffic slice. we also surfaced a telemetry hook you can use to measure effective cache hit by route
04:48 Diego: action: we'll share the canary runbook and the trace hook docs
04:56 Samir: for the network flap, our observability showed retries to the europe region. can we limit routing regionally to avoid cross-region retries?
05:10 Arjun: yes you can set region affinity policies and strict region-only routing, that will prevent spillover; tradeoff is capacity headroom if the region is saturated
05:26 Lena: ok curious about model variants — we've talked about moving to a 30b quant for quality. what's the cost uplift and perf?
05:38 Arjun: 30b quant will increase tokens per second cost and require larger memory. on Dedicated you can use better kernel selections and optimized kv handling to keep latencies tighter; quantitatively i'll show the delta in the bench results
05:54 Hannah: and in terms of contractual SLAs — if we go Dedicated, do we get an SLA on p95 latency or just uptime?
06:07 Maya: standard Dedicated contracts come with uptime SLAs; latency SLOs can be part of the SOW in enterprise deals. we'll map that to your success criteria in the pilot doc
06:20 Lena: success criteria for us: p95 < 800ms on average workload, sustained 200 qps with bursts to 400 with no greater than 2x cost increase over baseline, and security checklist -- SOC2, VPC peering, CMK encryption and audit logs retained 90 days
06:42 Diego: noted, i'll include those in the pilot acceptance criteria
06:48 Samir: question on autoscale — we saw slow spin-up during the last burst. can we pre-warm or provision buffer capacity?
06:59 Arjun: yes, Dedicated supports configurable headroom and burst pools; you can reserve a baseline pool and enable burst capacity which spins up faster since it's managed in the same tenant. hosted autoscale has more variable cold start behavior
07:18 Omar: what about observability — we need token-level cost and trace-ID correlation into our splunk stack
07:29 Diego: we have logging hooks for per-token meta and request traces; we can export to cloudwatch/splunk via our log sinks, or you can use the tracing API to capture request IDs and correlate with your systems
07:45 Hannah: finance question — what's the minimum commitment length for Dedicated and are there exit penalties?
07:55 Maya: typical commitments are 3/6/12 months. exit terms are negotiable on enterprise deals; for pilots we usually do month-to-month but show committed pricing if you decide to convert
08:09 Lena: timeline wise — we want to decide by end of March if we move to Dedicated for Q2. can we get the bench results and pricing by Mar 15?
08:18 Maya: yes that's doable. we'll send pricing scenarios by the 12th and lock the benchmark week for the 15-19 window pending Samir availability
08:29 Samir: we have a release freeze Mar 16, so prefer bench Mar 17 or 18
08:36 Arjun: noted, i'll tentatively book Mar 17 10-12 UTC for the 2-hour bench window
08:44 Diego: i'll add that to the calendar as provisional and share the runbook
08:50 Lena: a few quick technical clarifications — what quantization flavors do you support and do they break exactness for some of our downstream heuristics?
09:01 Arjun: we support int8 and int4 variants depending on model; int4 can sometimes change subtle output probability distributions causing slight tokenization differences. for deterministic downstream steps we recommend validating with your eval harness; we'll include eval results for your prompt set
09:20 Hannah: can you show an example of the forecasted bill with 30b vs 13b and with caching? even a sample spreadsheet helps
09:29 Maya: yes sample spreadsheet will be in the follow-up. we'll show unit cost per 1k tokens, estimated monthly token usage, and sensitivity to caching hit rates
09:40 Lena: on security docs — SOC2, network diag, SAML SSO steps, and a short runbook for KMS integration are must-haves. please include any 3rd-party pen test summary if you have it
09:52 Diego: we'll attach SOC2 summary and a redacted network diagram. third-party pentest summary is sensitive but we can share an exec summary under NDA if needed
10:06 Omar: small ask — can we enable stricter RBAC for routes and token scoping? we want dev/test to be isolated from prod lanes
10:18 Arjun: yep RBAC and token-level scope are supported; you can restrict routes, models, and allocate quotas per team. we'll share an RBAC matrix template
10:30 Hannah: finance wants a TOC for billing — if we convert to Dedicated mid-quarter, how does invoicing work? pro-rata adjustments?
10:41 Maya: pro-rata is standard; we'll provide sample invoice scenarios in the pricing doc. for committed deals we do monthly invoices with usage reconciliation if needed
10:54 Lena: any concerns about vendor lock-in? we may want the option to fallback to open-source runtime on prem later
11:05 Maya: we design routing and model pinning to be agnostic where possible; Private deployments are an option for air-gapped needs. also we provide model export guidance for some supported architectures — we'll discuss offline
11:20 Arjun: small note on quant and kernel selection — if you plan to move to 30b quant on Dedicated, we recommend enabling specialized kernels and a conservative batch size to avoid tail latencies
11:36 Samir: ok that's helpful. last operational ask — can we have a readout of any config changes from Feb that correlated with the incidents?
11:46 Diego: yes we'll attach a delta config log and a short root cause summary for the KV cache regression and the region failover event
11:58 Lena: great. to recap — deliver pricing spreadsheet by Mar 12, benchmark plan and runbook by Mar 15, bench window Mar 17-18, security artifacts immediately after call, and success criteria included in pilot doc
12:14 Maya: correct. i'll own pricing and coordinate with Product on SLO wording, Arjun will run bench, Diego will send runbooks and SOC2, Samir will give traffic patterns
12:29 Hannah: sounds good, thanks everyone
12:33 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up. end call
